title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — die actu ⇒ sinned actu; not Adam's act but original vitium inherent in each
pass_a_gloss: Tip argument: men die by act, so they have sinned by act—punishing in act for mere potency is absurd. They did not sin by act in Adam when he actually sinned. So another sin grounds their actual death: the original vice inherent in each and all, truly and properly by act, as certainly as it was in Adam himself. Tip before 'he sinned for all his posterity.'
pass_b_english: From which I argue thus: Men die by act. Therefore they have sinned by act. For it is absurd that one who has sinned only in potency, not in act, should be punished in act—and with a most heavy penalty. And yet they did not sin by act in Adam when he sinned actually. There must therefore be another sin because of which men die by act: namely that original vice which is in all and each truly and properly, by act, inherently—as certainly by act as it was in Adam himself.
source_text: Unde sic argumentor: Moriuntur homines actu. Ergo peccaverunt actu. Absurdum enim est ut qui potentia tantum peccavit, non autem actu, puniatur actu, & quidem poena gravissima. Atqui non peccaverunt actu in Adamo cum peccavit actualiter. Aliud igitur sit oportet peccatum ob quod actu moriantur homines, nempe vitium illud originale, quo quod omnibus & singulis inest vere & proprie, actu, inhaerenter; tam certe actu quam fuit in ipso Adamo.

choices.choice: Die actu⇒sinned actu; original vitium inherent
